svg.title: Green Sea ocean circulation: two inflows and a shared offshore outflow
svg.desc: Working model over an exact crop of taelgar-basemap.jpg. Reference coordinates use the original map scaled to 1907 by 1280. Blue cold water enters northeast and travels west close to the northern shore; orange warm water enters southeast, travels west and turns north west of Irrla. Teal shared flow returns east between Ursk and Irrla. Dashed eastern connectors denote exchange at unspecified depths, including beneath moving islands; crossings of island footprints never assert a surface channel. Seasonal effects are qualitative. Grey double-ended Gulf exchange leaves vertical ordering open. No wind arrows, pressure zones, or ship routes. North up; small hexes 24 statute miles face to face.

g.text: Cold northern inflow + warm southern inflow → shared eastward offshore outflow

svg.text: toward Ursk and the northwestern sea
surface slows where summer easterlies oppose it
westward, then north through the western basin

g.text: river plumes and seasonal coastal currents.
No permanent gulf-wide loop is assigned.
The fast northern current is not drawn
Strait depths and any layered exchange
Northern westerlies favor offshore eastward flow.
Winter cooling mixes the upper sea; spring opens the outward trade season.
Easterlies reinforce the fast westward coastal branch.
Opposing offshore surface flow slows; deeper / broader return continues.
Returning westerlies favor eastbound offshore passages.
Waves against a persisting coastal current can make late returns hazardous.
WATER MOVEMENT ONLY · Schematic corridors, not pilotage tracks or measured current speeds.
NORTH UP · SMALL HEXES: 24 MILES FACE TO FACE · BASEMAP: TAELGAR-BASEMAP.JPG
